key_insight: This paper introduces a simulation-free way to learn population dynamics directly from snapshots by using Wasserstein Lagrangian residuals. It expands beyond gradient-flow models to capture both conservative and periodic evolution in evolving distributions.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of reconstructing and extrapolating time-evolving probability distributions from unpaired observations without relying on costly numerical simulation, while also handling dynamics that are not purely dissipative.
method: Formulate population dynamics in Wasserstein space using a Lagrangian mechanics perspective.
Replace simulation-based training with residual-based learning, so the model is optimized directly from observed snapshots.
Enable learning of both gradient-flow and non-gradient-flow behavior, including conservative and periodic motion.
Avoid running a numerical solver at every training step, reducing computational overhead.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more scalable and flexible way to model evolving distributions from sparse observations. It is especially useful in scientific domains where dynamics may be cyclic, reversible, or otherwise incompatible with standard gradient-flow assumptions.
visual_elements: Timeline of distribution snapshots showing reconstruction and extrapolation over time
Side-by-side comparison of gradient flow vs. conservative/periodic dynamics in Wasserstein space
Pipeline diagram contrasting simulation-based training with residual-based training
Icon set for cells, fluids, and trajectories to illustrate application domains
paper_title: Simulation-Free Learning of Population Dynamics with Wasserstein Lagrangian Residuals
paper_authors: Fedor Sergeev, Markus Heinonen, Daniel Waxman, Tim Cooijmans, Ricardo Baptista
